nodes.label: R0 artefact staleness sweep
nodes.rationale: Scoped as a triage rather than a blanket regeneration because the log/57 staleness mechanism leaves a readable store_ceiling signature: reading the stamp is a complete test costing seconds, so regeneration is needed only where the stamp is wrong or absent.

nodes.label: store_ceiling stamp
nodes.rationale: warehouse.build() rebuilds from a CSV seed ending 2026-05-31, silently dropping June and 1-7 July rows, so a short store stamps 2026-05-31 instead of the true 2026-07-07. File mtimes are NOT evidence — many share a checkout timestamp.

nodes.label: Gate A ruler migration (VENUE_SCALE_BASIS)
nodes.rationale: Decision row 87 made config.VENUE_SCALE_BASIS the single authority; artefacts predating it carry the superseded calendar_lag7 basis. A denominator swap is rung-independent, so every mean moves by the same ratio and the ordering survives.

nodes.label: eval/occurrence_gate.py + occurrence_gate_beer_hall.json
nodes.rationale: Carried a hard-coded BASIS='calendar_lag7'; migrated to config.VENUE_SCALE_BASIS. Re-run moved both means by 0.819x inside log/70's band, and both arms stay in the 90% MCS set — the gate still does not measurably help.

nodes.label: metric_ordering.json — second Gate A casualty
nodes.rationale: Every conclusion in log/63 survives; every magnitude in it was wrong. The correction is APPENDED to log/63 rather than edited in, preserving the record.

nodes.label: The venv is part of an artefact's identity
nodes.rationale: A regeneration in .venv-forecast (no TSB-AD) degraded gracefully and silently replaced the whole seven-cell tab:vuspr table while leaving all other numbers intact — a diff that skimmed totals would have passed it. This is the argument for stamping BEFORE regenerating.

nodes.label: Inherited-stamp defect in the scaled report writer
nodes.rationale: _write_scaled_report inherited the base writer's stamp through split(_SCALED_MARKER)[0] and stranded a second identity block mid-document; it now strips an inherited stamp.

nodes.label: functional_pair.json 266-vs-260 origin count
nodes.rationale: Reproduces exactly, so not staleness — a design difference: 266 origins come from Ellel's untrimmed 392-row frame, 260 from the 386-row frame after trim_to_active. Recorded so a later session does not rediscover it as a staleness question.

nodes.label: The 392-against-386 frame distinction
nodes.rationale: Ellel's untrimmed calendar frame versus the frame after trim_to_active drops a leading dead span (the 2025-06-08 mis-ring plus 2025-06-09 to 06-13). Load-bearing across at least three artefacts, hence the standing instruction that every table states which frame it is on.
